relevance_note: Case report of an infant with familial HA20 whose TNFAIP3 nonsense variant was shared with her father: "The variant was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the infant and her father".
method_note: Read the full paper by hand; a Python script in the scratch directory only assembled the JSON and checked spans. Four in-scope people: the infant (label 'patient', rule 5; Fig. 2 calls her the proband), her father (TNFAIP3 carrier, affected), her mother (no variant testing reported; described as having no SLE/Sjogren's history and negative autoantibody tests; included as a tested relative) and her grandmother (affected relative; maternal or paternal side not stated; no genetic testing reported). Table 2 has ages as columns (header '| Tests | 2 mon | ... | 20 mon |'); age at last evaluation '20 mon' is the last follow-up column of Table 2, not an explicitly stated age at report. Age at onset '2-month-old' is the age at first presentation. No age at diagnosis is stated. Contradictions/inconsistencies: (1) the TNFAIP3 variant is called 'a definite pathogenic mutation' in the case description but 'likely pathogenic variant' in the Discussion and 'pathogenic variant' in the abstract; (2) anti-La is listed among 'positive autoantibodies' in the text but is 'Borderline' in Tables 1 and 2 (recorded as observed with the borderline detail); (3) the text says 'Her latest laboratory tests (Table 1)' although Table 1 is labelled initial tests. Father's zygosity and inheritance are not stated, so left 'not reported'; his transcript/protein are taken from the same variant's description because the paper says 'The variant was confirmed by Sanger sequencing in the infant and her father'. No functional assay was performed (authors: 'no additional functional study is necessary'); in silico MutationTaster/conservation data were not recorded as functional evidence. The NF1 variant (c.4103T>G, p.Leu1368*) is attributed to the infant unambiguously and recorded; the authors do not name its variant class. Low C3/C4, Hb 9.8 g/dL and weight/height percentiles are printed without the authors labelling them abnormal (except 'Levels of C3 and C4 improved'), so no hypocomplementemia, anemia or growth-failure rows were made; growth failure left 'not reported'. 'did not have arthritis' does not exclude 'arthritis or arthralgia', and 'did not have bloody diarrhea' does not exclude GI inflammation, so those checklist items are 'not reported'.
